A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Jenga video-generation acceleration work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality and latency measurements, component ablations, qualitative analyses and a user study with 70 valid responses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds mask and scheduling ablations, FVD evaluations, partitioning comparisons and additional model configurations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same attention carving, space-filling-curve partitioning, mask construction, progressive resolution, text amplification and timestep skipping procedures. The additional Turbo configurations reuse existing components; no new proposed algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 newly uses Inter4K videos as a real-data reference distribution for FVD evaluation. The existing VBench, VBench-I2V and Sora-prompt evaluations remain, with unchanged text-to-video and image-to-video task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 7 evaluates STA tiled-local partitioning and an optimized local partitioning strategy against 3D-SFC for padding and computational overhead. STA was previously discussed without this reported comparison. The established CLEAR, MInference, SVG and TeaCache comparator sets remain in the retained experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds FVD evaluation against Inter4K and differently seeded baseline generations, new mask and resolution-schedule controls, and Turbo configurations for AccVideo and Wan2.1. Table 4 also revises the reported three-stage selection rates from [0.7, 0.8, 0.8] to [0.3, 0.2, 0.2], without establishing that those experiments were rerun. Together these substantially extend the evaluation design; the original VBench and user-study protocols remain.

E4.justification: Tables 3c–d substantially extend the existing ablations with TopK-only and no-importance-mask controls, low-resolution step fractions from 10% to 90%, additional cutoff thresholds and effective-sparsity measurements. Appendix C.5 adds partitioning-overhead comparisons and a dynamic SFC scanning experiment reporting no quality improvement with roughly 20 seconds of additional overhead. Existing condition/adjacency-mask ablations are retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 retains the fixed-seed-per-prompt statement and newly describes FVD comparisons using different sampling seeds. This adds seed information for the new evaluation, without specifying seed identities, run counts or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. The existing latency error-bar reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical evidence in Tables 3c–d, 6 and 7 and an AttenCarve-plus-ProRes row in Table 1. Table 2 replaces AccVideo results of 76 seconds/83.39% VBench with 51 seconds/83.29%, and Wan2.1 results of 24 seconds/82.68% with 17 seconds/82.52%. Table 4 retains the earlier settings as Base and identifies the new results as Turbo, so these are configuration changes rather than same-setting gains. The detailed VBench table is unchanged after renumbering from 6 to 8.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, mask definitions, complexity statements and mathematical content of the algorithms are unchanged. The added empirical metrics and partitioning discussion introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution statements and conclusion retain the same training-free acceleration claims, complementary attention-carving/progressive-resolution contributions and headline 8.83× speedup. Additional supporting evaluations do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds interpretations of the importance mask, effective sparsity and the 50% low-resolution schedule. Appendix C.5 explains why initial noise and memory overhead discourage adaptive partitioning, and argues that Jenga could complement feature caching. Existing limitations concerning latent-resizing artifacts and static partitioning remain.

D1.justification: Table 4 adds parameter entries for the AccVideo and Wan2.1 Turbo configurations and revises the three-stage selection-rate list. Table 7 specifies video dimensions, block size and local partition shapes. Code-access information, hardware descriptions and pseudocode remain unchanged. Documentation is imperfect: the new Turbo rows list S=1 alongside changing resolution factors, while Appendix B.1 still describes Wan2.1 ProRes adaptation as future work.

R1.justification: v2 adds the AdaPool citation associated with Inter4K as reference 72; the previous 71 cited works are retained. Section 2 is unchanged, while Appendix C.5 expands positioning against STA/CLEAR partitioning and TeaCache feature reuse.

P1.justification: The revision adds localized explanatory paragraphs and subheadings in Section 4.3, Appendix C.5 and an acknowledgment, alongside small wording edits. The abstract, introduction, related-work section, method exposition and conclusion remain essentially unchanged, preserving the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands from two panels to four, Tables 1 and 4 gain rows, and new Tables 6–7 present FVD and partitioning results. The previous detailed Table 6 becomes Table 8 without changing its data. Existing figures are retained; Figure 7 moves and Figures 16–17 relocate after the references. These are localized display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The additional mask and scheduling ablations strengthen validation of design choices that v1 tested less directly, while the partitioning analysis and FVD results broaden the evidence. The benefit is limited by incomplete FVD sampling details and new reporting inconsistencies: AttenCarve-plus-ProRes has VBench 84.65% in Table 1 but 83.12% in Table 6, and the Turbo settings conflict with retained descriptions. Overall, v2 modestly strengthens the existing empirical case without resolving these reproducibility issues.
